findings.fix: Add `method="post"` to the form element: `<form id="form" method="post">`
findings.violation: Form lacks a method attribute, which defaults to GET. Account creation forms containing password fields should use POST to prevent credentials from appearing in browser history or server logs.

findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate fields, or clearly distinguish their purposes in the labels (e.g., rename "Your name" to something more specific like "Legal name on account").
findings.location: Full name field and Your name field
findings.violation: Two separate required fields both collect the user's name with different field names ("full_name" vs "legal_name"), creating ambiguity about whether they serve different purposes or are duplicates.

findings.fix: Add value attributes to each option: `<option value="standard">Standard</option><option value="express">Express</option>` etc.
findings.location: Preferred shipping speed select (rows containing "Standard", "Express", etc.)
findings.violation: Option elements have no value attributes, so the form will submit the display text as data instead of normalized values.

findings.evidence: `<label id="member-label" for="member-input">Membership number (8 digits)</label>` with `placeholder="Must be 8 digits"`
findings.fix: Add `pattern="[0-9]{8}" maxlength="8"` attributes to the input.
findings.violation: The label and placeholder both specify an 8-digit requirement, but the input lacks validation attributes (pattern, maxlength, minlength) to enforce it.

findings.evidence: `<label id="contacttime-label"...>Preferred contact time</label>` followed by `<input id="contacttime-input" name="contact_time" type="text" required="">`
findings.fix: Change `type="text"` to `type="time"`, or replace with a select element offering predefined options like "Morning", "Afternoon", "Evening".
findings.violation: A text input cannot properly capture a time preference; users have no guidance on format and the field accepts any text.

findings.fix: Move `style="font-size:16px"` to a CSS stylesheet and apply it via a class or selector.
findings.violation: Inline style is applied only to this input; other form fields lack this styling, and it should be managed in CSS for consistency.

findings.fix: Remove the inline style and apply `display: block` via CSS.
findings.violation: Inline style should be managed in a CSS stylesheet, not embedded in HTML.

findings.fix: Move inline styles to CSS and either add an onclick handler, title attribute, or remove the button if it serves no purpose.
findings.violation: Button has inline styles while the submit button does not, creating visual inconsistency; additionally, the button's purpose is unclear with no onclick handler visible.
